title: OpenAI ChatCompletions contract normalizer and streaming projection
creator: Maya Thompson
description: We need a deterministic mapping layer that translates inbound OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/legacy) requests and streaming responses into Redwood's canonical streaming + function-calling shape. This ticket implements the request normalizer and response projector used by hosted and Dedicated gateways so legacy clients get correct structured outputs, function-call semantics, and provenance metadata while preserving streaming guarantees and failure modes. Key responsibilities: 1) Normalize role/message shapes, system/content splitting, and temperature/stop parameter semantics; 2) Map streaming delta frames (choice.delta) into Redwood SSE frames with consistent event types (token, tool_call_start, tool_call_update, tool_call_finish, finish_reason); 3) Reconcile OpenAI finish_reason and choice indices with Redwood's per-request outcome model; 4) Surface function/tool calling as explicit tool events while preserving ordered partial content for clients that expect content-first delivery; 5) Ensure idempotent replay/partial-reconnect semantics for resumed streams (cursor + sequence numbers); 6) Translate function responses (including multi-step function_call->function_response sequences) into structured messages or synthetic tool events based on runtime policy. This is intended to reduce downstream adapter code and fix longstanding mismatches observed in client integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Inbound OA ChatCompletions request examples (including messages array, function signatures, and stop tokens) are correctly normalized into Redwood canonical request format for >95% of observed shapes.

Streaming behavior: when OA sends SSE deltas, clients connected to Redwood receive token events in the same order with an added set of tool_call_* events for function invocation and a final finish_reason mapping.

Function calling: OA's function_call suggestion frames are emitted as tool_call_start + tool_call_update* + tool_call_finish, and a subsequent function_response is attached to the conversation as a structured message with provenance metadata.
Partial reconnect: clients that reconnect with the same request_id can resume from last-seen sequence number and receive consistent deltas; no duplicate tokens after resume in >=99% of test replays.
Backward compatibility: legacy OA consumers receive expected fields (choices, index, finish_reason) in the non-streaming proxy path with deterministic mapping rules documented in the spec.
E2E tests: harness with 15 OA-like samples (edge cases included) passes streaming + resume + function-call test matrix on CI.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Maya T.: Initial ticket created after customer incident where a third-party SDK misinterpreted OA function_call deltas and triggered duplicate tool invocations. Collected 12 sample request/response traces from logs.

2026-02-24 - Ethan R.: Spike completed. Found three recurring mismatch classes: (1) choice.delta merging vs token-by-token, (2) OA includes function_call.name in separate delta events, (3) finish_reason semantics differ for truncated streams. Proposed model: explicit tool_call lifecycle events with sequence numbers.

2026-02-28 - Design review: Agreed on event taxonomy (token, tool_call_start, tool_call_update, tool_call_finish, function_response_message, final_outcome). UX asked to include a small "compatibility_hint" header for clients to opt into OA-shaped envelopes.

2026-03-03 - Implementation note: Added a lightweight request hash to support idempotent replay and a monotonic sequence counter per request. This will be persisted in the gateway memory for 60s and in Redis for long-lived Dedicated sessions.

2026-03-07 - QA: Found race where tool_call_update followed immediately by tool_call_finish caused an out-of-order delivery if batching is enabled. Temporary mitigation: drain buffer on tool_call_finish events; long-term: adjust batch window and include event watermarks.
2026-03-10 - Ethan R.: PR opened (see links). Plan to run canary for hosted API with OA-compat flag enabled for 10% of traffic next week.
